title: Seasonal Variation in Energy Expenditure, Water Turnover, and Physical Activity in Adults
official: Impacts of Seasonal Environmental Variation on Energy Expenditure, Water Turnover, and Physical Activity
summary: This prospective observational study will investigate seasonal variation in total energy expenditure, water turnover, and physical activity in healthy adults living in or near Aberdeen, Scotland. Participants will complete two approximately 14-day measurement periods, one in winter and one in summer. Total energy expenditure and water turnover will be assessed using the doubly labelled water method, while physical activity and personal environmental exposure will be measured using wearable devices. The study will examine within-person differences between winter and summer and explore whether environmental factors, including ambient temperature, daylight, and sunlight exposure, are associated with changes in energy expenditure, water turnover, and physical activity.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Healthy adults aged 18-50 years Body mass index (BMI) of 18.5-29.9 kg/m² Available to participate in both winter (January/February) and summer (July/August) measurement periods Resident in or near Aberdeen, or spending most of the year in Scotland during the study period

Exclusion Criteria:

Any condition limiting normal daily physical activity Engagement in high-intensity training, including professional athletes History of bariatric surgery, current weight-loss interventions, or significant recent weight change (\>5 kg in the previous 6 months) Pregnancy, breastfeeding, planning pregnancy, irregular menstrual cycles, or menopause Any medical condition that may affect metabolism, physical activity, water balance, or study safety, including diabetes, uncontrolled thyroid disease, significant heart or kidney disease, or respiratory disease that limits normal activity Any psychiatric condition that may affect participation, daily activity, appetite, or ability to follow study procedures Use of medications or treatments that may significantly affect metabolism, appetite, body weight, or physical activity, including weight-loss medications, corticosteroids, diuretics, or stimulant medications Inability to provide informed consent Any condition judged by the investigators to compromise participant safety or data quality
